outOfScope: a general survey of object-oriented design

claims.claim: A class statement creates a class object and its suite becomes the class namespace.
Calling a class creates a new instance, and attributes can be read with dotted notation.
An instance method receives the instance when called through that instance; the conventional first parameter name is self.
An assignment such as self.name creates or changes an instance attribute, so different instances can hold different values.
A class attribute is shared through the class unless an instance attribute of the same name shadows it; mutable class attributes can unintentionally be shared.
Every Python object has an identity, type, and value.
